Hi Maria — great to meet you over video earlier. Appreciate the clear asks; I've drafted two short options below (plain-language) that you can slot into your evaluation doc.

Option A (explicit triggers):
"Redwood uses trusted subprocessors (e.g., cloud providers, analytics partners) for hosting, monitoring, and supporting the service. We only route customer requests outside your region for failover or capacity reasons; such routing is covered by contractual safeguards and encryption in transit and at rest. Customers on Dedicated or Private deployments can restrict or review subprocessors via our console and procurement process."

Option B (shorter):
"We may engage subprocessors (hosting, monitoring) to operate the service. Requests are routed based on capacity and failover needs; cross-border transfers are protected by encryption and contractual safeguards. Contact your account rep to discuss region-restricted deployments or subprocessors."

Notes / quick answers to your questions:
- Customers cannot fully opt out of all subprocessors on Hosted tier, but Dedicated/Private options allow greater control.
- We propose adding a small \"Region routing\" line near the data residency toggle in the console that links to more detail.

I've attached a text file with the Option A/B blurb (proposed-console-blurb-v1.txt). Laura — looping you in for legal/term language and to suggest any must-have phrasing. Jonas — please flag any product UI constraints for the console link.

Best,

Thanks for drafting these, Camila — useful starting point. A few legal edits and recommendations: 

- Avoid \"we may\" when talking about transfers in the primary console snippet; that phrasing reads as permissive. Prefer: "We may route requests outside the region only for failover or capacity reasons subject to safeguards."

- Add an explicit reference to contractual safeguards: "cross-border transfers are protected by contractual clauses (Standard Contractual Clauses or equivalent) and encryption in transit and at rest." That helps procurement triage quickly.

- For the opt-out language: Hosted tier customers cannot opt out of subprocessors that are required for service operation. Suggest: "Hosted customers: some subprocessors are required to operate the service and cannot be opted out of; contact sales to discuss Dedicated or Private deployment options for greater control."

- UI placement: we should keep the console blurb to one sentence and link to a longer DPA/FAQ. Suggest a 1-sentence primary blurb plus a "Learn more" link to a DPA/FAQ page that includes the list of subprocessors and an explanation of routing and safeguards.

Suggested primary blurb (legal-friendly, single sentence):
"Redwood may engage subprocessors to operate the service; requests will be routed across regions only for failover or capacity purposes and in such cases are protected by contractual safeguards and encryption."

If you want, I can mark up the console copy with inline annotations for procurement. Also, we should include guidance for the privacy and security reviewers on where the subprocessor list lives (our public subprocessor map + request process).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference
